model.name: Decision / Rationale
model.purpose: Represent a governed decision as an accountable aggregate. This bounded pass specifies the governance, participation and lifecycle surface only: who was mandated to decide, who took part and under what integrity conditions, how the decision moved from submission to approval and through its validity states, how its versions and provenance are controlled, and how it is classified, sealed, retained and defensibly disposed of.
model.scope_statement: In scope is the governance wrapper around the decision aggregate root: mandate and deciding authority, delegation, accountable roles, participation and applicable decision rule, declared interests and recusal, approval and ratification bindings, status and validity states, review/appeal/reopening, version and change history, provenance of the governed content, access classification and disclosure, integrity anchoring, retention, legal hold and disposition. The decision problem, alternatives, criteria, evaluation and outcome remain owned by the core area of this model; rationale, arguments, assumptions, dissent and explanation remain owned by the reasoning area. Approval activities, carrying records, legal judgments, claims, evidence and executable policies are referenced neighbours whose internal structures are not reproduced here.
in_scope: Deciding authority identity and the mandate instrument that authorises the decision
Delegation and sub-delegation chains with ceilings and validity windows
Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer assignments over the decision record
Participant roster with declared roles and the applicable decision rule and quorum attestation
Declared interests, conflict determinations and recusal actions
Submission, review, approval and ratification stage bindings to external approval activity records
Status and validity states including effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired and reopened
Review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening triggers and windows
Version identity, supersession and consolidation, and an append-only change ledger
Provenance of the governed decision content: attribution, derivation, attestation and capture mode
Access classification, exemption grounds, partial access and embargo
Fixity, sealing and non-repudiation references, and links to external audit trails
Retention schedule bindings, legal hold state, disposition authorisation, tombstone and archival transfer
out_of_scope: The decision problem statement, alternatives, criteria and evaluation results (core area of this model)
Rationale text, argument structure, assumptions, sensitivity, dissent content and explanation renditions (reasoning area of this model)
Execution of approval activities, their scheduling, assignment and completion semantics (WM-ACT-024)
Record carrier structure, repository classification and execution of retention and disposal actions (WM-REC-010)
Judicial reasoning, orders, remedies and court procedure (WM-POL-021)
Claim structure and evidence appraisal, quality and chain-of-custody semantics (WM-KNW-007, WM-KNW-008)
Authoring, evaluation, execution and enforcement of policies and executable rules
Audit-trail generation and retention of event logs by the systems that hold them
Person and organisation master identity, appointment and payroll data
Implementation project delivery, task execution and outcome measurement data

boundary_notes.distinction: Governance answers who could decide, under what conditions and with what validity; core answers what was decided among which alternatives against which criteria. Governance may reference dr-core-art-drg, dr-core-art-rule-table and dr-core-art-comparison-matrix by identifier but never restates the problem, options, criteria weights or evaluation results.

Governance carries only pointers to dr-rsn-art-statement-of-reasons, dr-rsn-art-argument-structure, dr-rsn-art-assumption-register, dr-rsn-art-sensitivity-record, dr-rsn-art-dissent-record, dr-rsn-art-explanation-rendition and dr-rsn-art-reasoning-trace. Dissent content, argument structure and evidence binding semantics stay in the reasoning area; governance records only that a dissent artefact exists and how it is disclosed and retained.

This model records the stage a decision reached and the identifier of the approval or ratification act. Activity initiation, assignment, execution, completion and any workflow engine state belong to WM-ACT-024.

This model states the retention schedule binding, hold state and disposition authorisation for the decision. The record carrier, its repository placement and the physical execution of destruction, transfer or migration belong to WM-REC-010 and the adopting Dimension's records authority.
A judicial or tribunal determination that resolves an appeal is referenced as an external judgment. Court composition, pleadings, orders, remedies and judicial reasoning are not modelled here.

An inbound reference: a change request is resolved by a decision. This model stores only the resolved change-request identifier and resolution timestamp; change-request intake, triage, states and closure remain with WM-ACT-032.

A decision may be constrained by, or may establish, a policy. Rule authoring, runtime evaluation, obligation discharge and enforcement are external. Referencing an evaluator never grants this model evaluation or enforcement semantics.

This model records fixity values, seal and signature references and an identifier that links to the external trail. Generation, protection, review and retention of audit records are owned by the system implementing the audit and accountability controls.

Participants, authorities and role holders are carried as references to party identifiers. Person and organisation master data, credentials and appointment records are not duplicated here; only the declared role in this decision is local.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Establishes records characteristics (authenticity, reliability, integrity, usability), metadata for records, assigned responsibilities, records controls, appraisal and disposition — the normative basis for governance, custody and disposition findings.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines Entity/Activity/Agent and the qualified patterns for delegation, attribution, association with roles, revision, derivation and invalidation — the alignment basis for delegation chains, role-qualified participation and content provenance.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0. Part 1: XML Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Provides FRBR work/expression/manifestation/item identification, lifecycle and eventRef tracking, temporalData, workflow metadata and TLC references for persons, roles and organisations — the alignment basis for version identity, lifecycle events and declared participant roles.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), United States
sources.relevance: Organises electronic records requirements into Capture, Maintenance and Use, Disposal, Transfer, Metadata and Reporting, separating program from system requirements and mandatory from preferred — the basis for retention, disposition, transfer and governance metadata expectations.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Defines issuer as the asserting authority, validFrom/validUntil validity windows, credentialStatus for revocation and suspension, and termsOfUse restrictions — the alignment basis for authority attribution, validity windows and suspended/revoked status semantics.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), United States
sources.version_or_date: Rev. 5, September 2020 (updates through December 2020; control catalog release 5.2.0, 27 August 2025)
sources.relevance: Control families for Audit and Accountability (audit records, non-repudiation), Access Control (access enforcement) and System and Information Integrity (information retention and disposal) — the basis for treating audit trails and enforcement as externally owned while this model holds references and classifications.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires an explicit time-offset of 'Z' or +/-HH:MM, defines the seconds field including leap seconds, and reserves '-00:00' for an unknown local offset — the normative basis for the timestamp rule and for separating event, observation and ingestion times.

sources.title: RFC 2026 (BCP 9): The Internet Standards Process -- Revision 3
sources.relevance: Documents maturity states, revision of a specification through the full process, retirement to Historic status, and a tiered conflict-resolution and appeals procedure with a two-month submission limit — the basis for status transitions, supersession and appeal/reconsideration windows.

sources.title: Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 regarding public access to European Parliament, Council and Commission documents
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: Article 4 exemption grounds including protection of an institution's decision-making process, Article 4(6) partial access by releasing non-exempt parts, Article 9 sensitive-document handling with originator consent, Article 11 public registers of documents, and the duty to give written reasons for refusal — a jurisdictional profile for access classification and disclosure exceptions.

sources.title: ELI ontology (European Legislation Identifier)
sources.organization: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.relevance: Defines in_force, consolidates/consolidated_by, changes/changed_by, repeals/repealed_by, responsibility_of_agent and passed_by over FRBR-style legal resources and expressions — the alignment basis for effective/superseded/repealed states, consolidation and authority attribution.

sources.title: Council Decision of 1 December 2009 adopting the Council's Rules of Procedure (2009/937/EU)
sources.relevance: Article 11 requires the presence of a majority of members entitled to vote and permits a member to act on behalf of not more than one other member; Article 12 provides written and silence procedures; Article 13 governs minutes recording decisions and statements — a concrete primary basis for quorum attestation, proxy representation, decision rule and participation mode.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), consolidated text
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation with an archiving derogation, Article 17 right to erasure and the Article 17(3) exceptions for legal obligations, public-interest tasks, archiving and legal claims, and Article 30 records of processing — the profile that constrains when erasure overrides tombstone-first deletion.

bundles.name: Decision authority, mandate and participation
bundles.description: Establishes who was competent to take the decision, under which mandate and delegation, who is accountable for the resulting record, who participated in which declared role, and what integrity conditions applied to that participation.
bundles.rationale: A decision is only authoritative if the deciding body acted within a mandate and the participation conditions prescribed for it. ISO 15489-1 makes assigned responsibilities and mandate-driven records requirements a precondition of authoritative evidence; PROV qualifies responsibility, association and delegation; the Council's Rules of Procedure show mandate, quorum and proxy representation as explicit, recorded facts.

layers.name: Mandate, deciding authority and accountable roles
layers.description: The competence chain: the authority that decided, the instrument that empowered it, the delegations exercised beneath it, and the standing roles accountable for the decision record afterwards.

findings.name: Deciding authority and mandate binding
findings.description: Identifies the body, office or role that took the decision and binds it to the mandate instrument, its subject and jurisdictional limits, its validity window and its succession path. Records the authority as an attributable agent rather than as free text.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates the body or office that took this decision, and under which mandate instrument did it act?
answer_data: Deciding authority reference resolved against the party or governing-body register
Mandate instrument reference with its issuing authority
Statement of which system of record issued the authority identifier

questions.text: What subject-matter, monetary or jurisdictional limits does the mandate place on this authority, and what is the recorded consequence of acting outside them?
answer_data: Enumerated mandate scope limits with units where quantified
Ultra vires handling code and the status the decision takes if a limit is breached
Reference to the reviewing forum competent to determine the breach

questions.text: Over which validity window was the mandate in force at the instant the decision was taken?
answer_data: Mandate validity start and end as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset
Decision event time compared against that window
Flag indicating whether the comparison was asserted or externally verified

questions.text: Which alternate or successor authority becomes responsible if the deciding body is dissolved, merged or renamed?
answer_data: Successor authority reference with the transfer instrument reference
Effective time of the succession
Retained historical authority reference for the original decision

data_elements.name: Deciding authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the body, office or role that took the decision, resolved against the authoritative party or governing-body register.

data_elements.name: Mandate instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the statute, charter, terms of reference, delegation instrument or standing order that confers competence for this decision.

data_elements.name: Mandate scope limit
data_elements.description: A declared limit on the mandate expressed as subject-matter, monetary ceiling, geography or term.

data_elements.name: Mandate validity window
data_elements.description: Start and end instants during which the mandate was in force, each an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Authority succession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the successor or alternate authority and to the instrument effecting the succession.

artifacts.name: Decision authority and delegation register
artifacts.description: A governed register of deciding authorities, their mandate instruments, scope limits, validity windows and the delegations issued beneath them, against which any individual decision's authority claim is resolved. It is a register of competence, not a record of decisions taken.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identity is taken from the authoritative master-system identifier of the governing-body or decision-rights register maintained by the adopting Dimension; failing that, a governed IRI assigned by a recognised registry; failing both, a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension and flagged as Dimension-assigned. Register entries are keyed by authority identifier plus mandate instrument identifier, never by adoption date or meeting name.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and proxy representation
findings.description: Records the chain from the mandate holder to the person or system that actually exercised the decision, with the ceiling and validity window on each step, whether sub-delegation was permitted, and how a vote or act exercised on behalf of another participant is captured.

questions.text: Which delegation or sub-delegation steps link the mandate holder to the agent that actually exercised this decision?
answer_data: Ordered delegation chain entries, each naming delegator, delegate and instrument
Qualified delegation reference aligned to the PROV delegation pattern
Indicator of whether each step was standing or ad hoc

questions.text: What ceiling applies to each delegation step, and is further sub-delegation permitted at that step?
answer_data: Ceiling value and unit per step
Sub-delegation permitted flag with the authorising clause reference
Escalation target when the ceiling is exceeded

questions.text: How is a delegation revoked or withdrawn, and what is the effect on decisions already taken under it?
answer_data: Revocation instrument reference and effective instant
Retrospectivity code stating whether prior decisions remain valid
Ratification requirement flag for acts taken after revocation

questions.text: When an act or vote was exercised on behalf of another participant, how is that representation recorded?
answer_data: Proxy entry naming represented party, representing party and the authorising provision
Limit on the number of parties one participant may represent
Whether the proxy counted towards the participation threshold

data_elements.name: Delegation chain entry
data_elements.description: One step of delegated competence, naming delegator, delegate, instrument reference and ordinal position in the chain.

data_elements.name: Delegation ceiling
data_elements.description: The quantified limit attached to a delegation step, with value, unit and basis.

data_elements.name: Delegation validity window
data_elements.description: Start and end instants of a delegation step as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Delegation revocation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instrument revoking or withdrawing a delegation, with its retrospectivity code.

data_elements.name: Proxy representation entry
data_elements.description: Record that one participant acted on behalf of another, naming both parties and the authorising provision.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Delegation facts are short reference structures resolved against dr-gov-art-authority-register and mirrored into the lifecycle ledger; they carry no independent document body. The delegation instrument itself is a document owned and published by the issuing authority, so materialising a second artefact here would duplicate an external record and create a competing copy of a mandate this model does not own.

findings.name: Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer assignment
findings.description: Assigns the standing accountabilities over the decision record after it is taken: who owns it, who maintains its governance metadata, who holds physical or logical custody of its projections, and who is obliged to review it. Distinguishes accountability for governance metadata from accountability for the substance of the decision.

questions.text: Who is the accountable owner of this decision record, and how does that accountability differ from those of the steward, custodian and reviewer?
answer_data: Party references for owner, steward, custodian and reviewer
Responsibility statement per role drawn from the adopting Dimension's role catalogue
Indicator of whether a role is held by a person, an office or an organisational unit

questions.text: Which role is answerable for the accuracy of the governance metadata as distinct from the correctness of the decision itself?
answer_data: Named role accountable for governance metadata accuracy
Named authority accountable for decision substance
Escalation path when the two disagree

questions.text: How is a role assignment transferred when the holder leaves, and from which instant does the successor's accountability run?
answer_data: Handover event reference with predecessor and successor party references
Handover effective instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z
Whether the predecessor retains residual accountability for the prior period

questions.text: Which role holds the authority to release this decision to a wider audience or to publish it?
answer_data: Release authority role reference
Constraint stating whether release requires the deciding authority's concurrence
Reference to the access schedule entry that the release must satisfy

data_elements.name: Governance owner reference
data_elements.description: Party or office accountable for the decision record as a governed asset.

data_elements.name: Steward reference
data_elements.description: Party accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the decision's governance metadata.

data_elements.name: Custodian reference
data_elements.description: Party holding custody of a stored projection of the decision record.

data_elements.name: Reviewer reference
data_elements.description: Party or forum obliged to review the decision at scheduled or triggered intervals.

data_elements.name: Role handover entry
data_elements.description: Transfer of a named role from predecessor to successor with its effective instant and residual-accountability flag.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role assignments are reference tuples pointing at party identifiers held in an external identity model; they have no document body of their own and change independently of the decision content. Materialising them as an artefact would create a stale local copy of party master data and a second, competing source of truth for accountability that the adopting Dimension's role catalogue already owns.

layers.name: Participation, decision rule and integrity of participation
layers.description: Who took part in which declared capacity, under which decision rule and participation threshold, and what was declared, determined and acted upon regarding conflicts of interest.

findings.name: Participant roster, declared roles and applicable decision rule
findings.description: Captures the participants and their declared roles, the entitlement to vote or object, the decision rule that governed the taking of the decision, the mode of proceeding, and the attestation that any required participation threshold was met.

questions.text: Which participants took part, in which declared roles, and which of them were entitled to vote or formally object?
answer_data: Participant entries with party reference and declared role code
Voting entitlement flag per participant
Alignment of role codes to a controlled role vocabulary such as a top-level role classification

questions.text: Which decision rule applied — unanimity, qualified or simple majority, consensus, silence or written procedure — and where is that rule prescribed?
answer_data: Decision rule code from a controlled vocabulary
Reference to the rules of procedure clause prescribing it
Threshold expression where the rule is numeric

questions.text: Was the participation threshold or quorum asserted as satisfied, by whom, and on what stated basis?
answer_data: Quorum attestation with attesting party reference and attestation instant
Counted and required participation figures as asserted
Explicit statement that this is the presiding authority's assertion, not an evaluation performed by this model

questions.text: How is a decision taken by written or silence procedure distinguished from one taken in a convened sitting?
answer_data: Participation mode code covering convened, written, silence and delegated modes
Objection window for silence procedure with its closing instant
Reference to the minutes or proceedings record where one exists

questions.text: How is an abstention or formal objection referenced without reproducing the dissent record owned by the reasoning area?
answer_data: Abstention or objection event entry with participant reference and instant
Pointer to dr-rsn-art-dissent-record by identifier only
Rule stating that dissent content, arguments and grounds are not stored here

data_elements.name: Participant entry
data_elements.description: One participant with party reference, declared role code, voting entitlement flag and attendance or response state.

data_elements.name: Decision rule code
data_elements.description: Controlled code naming the rule under which the decision was taken, with a reference to the prescribing provision.

data_elements.name: Quorum attestation
data_elements.description: Assertion by a named presiding party that the participation threshold was satisfied, with counted and required figures and the attestation instant.

data_elements.name: Participation mode code
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing convened sitting, written procedure, silence procedure and delegated exercise.

data_elements.name: Dissent record reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only pointer to the dissent artefact owned by the reasoning area; no dissent content is stored locally.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The participation surface is a roster of references plus a small set of coded assertions; the narrative proceedings that would justify a document already exist as minutes or a proceedings record owned by the convening body and, where reasoning is involved, as the reasoning area's artefacts. Holding these facts inline keeps them queryable and avoids creating a rival account of the sitting that this model has no authority to issue.

findings.name: Declared interests, conflict determination and recusal
findings.description: Records interests declared by participants before or during the decision, who determined whether a declared interest was disqualifying, the recusal or mitigation action taken, and the effect of recusal on the applicable participation threshold.

questions.text: Which interests were declared by participants in relation to this decision, and against which register entry was each declaration recorded?
answer_data: Interest declaration entries with declaring party, interest type and declaration instant
Reference to the interests register entry where one is maintained
Indicator of whether the declaration was standing or decision-specific

questions.text: Who determined that a declared interest was disqualifying, and what recusal or mitigation action followed?
answer_data: Determining party reference and determination instant
Determination outcome code and stated grounds reference
Recusal or mitigation action code such as withdrawal, non-participation in the vote, or supervised participation

questions.text: How does a recusal change the participation threshold or decision rule applied to the affected item?
answer_data: Adjusted threshold figures after recusal
Statement of whether the recused participant counted towards presence
Reference to the provision governing the adjustment

questions.text: For how long must interest declarations and conflict determinations remain retrievable after the decision is closed, and under what lawful basis?
answer_data: Retention period reference for declarations, separate from the decision's own period
Lawful basis reference where the declarations contain personal data
Masking or minimisation requirement applicable at disclosure

data_elements.name: Interest declaration entry
data_elements.description: A declared interest with declaring party reference, interest type code, declaration instant and optional register entry reference.

data_elements.name: Conflict determination
data_elements.description: The determination on a declared interest, naming the determining party, outcome code, grounds reference and determination instant.

data_elements.name: Recusal action code
data_elements.description: Coded action taken in consequence of a disqualifying interest, such as withdrawal, abstention from the vote or supervised participation.

data_elements.name: Recusal effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the recusal took effect, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Declaration personal-data flag
data_elements.description: Indicator that a declaration contains personal data and is therefore subject to minimisation and to a lawful-basis-bound retention period.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Declarations and determinations are short, strongly typed assertions that must remain individually queryable for threshold recomputation and disclosure masking, and they frequently contain personal data whose minimisation is easier to enforce at field level than in a document body. Where a jurisdiction requires a standing register of interests, that register is an external instrument owned by the integrity authority and is referenced rather than reissued here.

bundles.name: Approval, status lifecycle and change control
bundles.description: How the decision moved from submission through review to approval or ratification, which validity state it holds and why, how it may be reviewed, appealed, reconsidered or reopened, and how its versions, changes and content provenance are controlled.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative decision records require an explicit, transition-controlled state model with recorded effective dating, a supersession and consolidation chain, and attributable change history. RFC 2026 demonstrates staged maturity, retirement to a historic state and a bounded appeals procedure; the ELI ontology supplies in-force, consolidation and repeal relations; Akoma Ntoso supplies FRBR-level version identity and lifecycle events; PROV-O supplies attribution, revision and invalidation.

layers.name: Submission, approval, status and reconsideration
layers.description: The approval pipeline binding, the controlled status and validity model with its effective dating and conditions, and the triggers and windows for review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening.

findings.name: Submission, review and approval stage binding
findings.description: Records which governance stages the decision passed, which are mandatory before it can take effect, and the identifier of the external approval or ratification activity that evidences each stage. Distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement.

questions.text: Which submission, review, approval and ratification stages did this decision pass, and which of them are mandatory before it can take effect?
answer_data: Ordered stage entries with stage code, outcome code and completion instant
Mandatory-stage flag per stage
Reference to the procedure that prescribes the stage sequence

questions.text: Which external approval activity record evidences each stage, and which identifier binds the two?
answer_data: Approval activity reference per stage resolved against WM-ACT-024
Binding identifier and the resolution method for it
Statement that activity execution and completion semantics are not held locally

questions.text: What distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement in this governance context?
answer_data: Definitions of approval, ratification and endorsement as used by the adopting Dimension
Legal or procedural effect of each on the decision's validity
Which of them can retrospectively cure an act taken beyond delegated authority

questions.text: What happens to the decision when a mandatory stage is skipped, completed out of order, or completed by an unauthorised party?
answer_data: Defect code and the status assigned to a defectively approved decision
Remediation path such as ratification, re-submission or withdrawal
Notification obligation and its addressee

data_elements.name: Approval stage entry
data_elements.description: One governance stage with stage code, mandatory flag, outcome code, deciding party reference and completion instant.

data_elements.name: Approval activity reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to the external approval or ratification activity record that evidences a stage.

data_elements.name: Approval defect code
data_elements.description: Coded defect in the approval pipeline, such as a skipped mandatory stage or an unauthorised approver.

data_elements.name: Ratification reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a ratifying act that cures a defect or confirms an act taken under delegated or urgent procedure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Stages are carried as thin bindings to approval activity records that live in WM-ACT-024; the substantive approval evidence, including approver identity, execution and completion, is that model's artefact. Creating a governance document for the pipeline here would reproduce an approval record this model does not own and would introduce a second, divergent statement of whether approval occurred.

findings.name: Status, validity and conditional effectiveness
findings.description: Holds the controlled status of the decision and its permitted transitions, the separation of approval, publication and effective instants, the conditions attached to a conditional decision and who confirms them, and identifier-only references to follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations.

questions.text: Which status does this decision hold now, and which controlled vocabulary defines the permitted values and the legal transitions between them?
answer_data: Current status code from the governed status vocabulary covering draft, submitted, approved, effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired and reopened
Transition table naming permitted source and target states
Authority competent to perform each transition

questions.text: From which instant is the decision effective, and how does that differ from the instants at which it was approved and published?
answer_data: Effective instant, approval instant and publication instant as separate RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offsets or Z
Indicator of retrospective effect where the effective instant precedes approval
Ingestion instant recorded separately from all three

questions.text: Which conditions precedent or subsequent must hold for a conditional decision to become or remain effective, and who confirms their satisfaction?
answer_data: Condition entries with condition text reference, type and due instant
Confirming party reference and confirmation instant
Consequence code applied when a condition fails

questions.text: Which follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations are attached by reference, and which model owns their execution?
answer_data: Follow-up obligation references with obligation type and owning model identifier
Reporting-back instant or interval where one is stipulated
Explicit statement that implementation progress and outcome measurement are not stored here

questions.text: What causes automatic expiry as opposed to explicit revocation or suspension, and how is each distinguished in the record?
answer_data: Expiry rule reference and the computed or stipulated expiry instant
Revocation and suspension entries with acting authority, ground code and effective instant
Rule preventing an expired decision from being silently treated as revoked

data_elements.name: Status code
data_elements.description: Current governed status of the decision drawn from the controlled status vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Status transition entry
data_elements.description: A recorded transition with source status, target status, acting authority reference, ground code and effective instant.

data_elements.name: Effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the decision has effect, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z, held separately from approval and publication instants.

data_elements.name: Effectiveness condition entry
data_elements.description: A condition precedent or subsequent with type, due instant, confirming party reference and satisfaction state.

data_elements.name: Follow-up obligation reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to an implementation or monitoring obligation arising from the decision, together with the model that owns its execution.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status, effective dating and conditions are the queryable control fields that determine whether the decision may be relied upon at a given instant, so they must be first-class inline data rather than text inside a document. Follow-up obligations are deliberately reference-only because implementation progress, monitoring results and outcome measurement are executed and evidenced by other models; issuing an artefact here would invite those execution facts to accumulate locally.

findings.name: Review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening
findings.description: Defines what triggers a scheduled or event-driven review, who may appeal or seek reconsideration to which forum within what time limit, on what grounds a closed decision may be reopened and what status it then takes, and how a review outcome is linked to the original decision without overwriting it.

questions.text: What triggers a scheduled or event-driven review of this decision, and by which due instant must the review occur?
answer_data: Review trigger code covering fixed interval, condition breach, external change and complaint
Review due instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z
Party obliged to initiate the review

questions.text: Who may appeal or request reconsideration, to which forum, and within what time limit from which starting instant?
answer_data: Eligible appellant classes and the forum reference for each escalation tier
Time limit expressed as a duration with the instant from which it runs
Whether the forum's determination is final on procedure, on merits, or on both

questions.text: On what grounds may a closed decision be reopened, and which status does it hold while reopened?
answer_data: Reopening ground codes such as new evidence, procedural defect or material change of circumstance
Status held during reopening and whether the original remains effective meanwhile
Authority competent to authorise the reopening

questions.text: How is the outcome of a review, appeal or reconsideration linked to the original decision without overwriting it?
answer_data: Outcome reference with relation type such as confirms, varies, remits or quashes
Reference to an external legal judgment where the forum is judicial
Rule that the original version remains retrievable in its approved form

data_elements.name: Review trigger code
data_elements.description: Coded reason a review becomes due, whether periodic, conditional or event-driven.

data_elements.name: Review due time
data_elements.description: Instant by which a due review must be conducted, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Appeal window
data_elements.description: Duration within which an appeal or reconsideration request must be lodged, with the instant from which it runs.

data_elements.name: Appeal forum reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the forum competent to hear an appeal at a given escalation tier.

data_elements.name: Review outcome reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the reviewing or appellate determination, with the relation it bears to the original decision.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Triggers, windows, forums and outcome links are scheduling and relationship data that must drive obligations and queries rather than be read out of a document. The substantive review or appellate determination is itself a decision or a legal judgment owned by another record, so this finding deliberately holds only the pointer and the relation type and creates no artefact that could be mistaken for the determination.

layers.name: Version history and provenance of decision content

bundles.name: Access, integrity and defensible disposition

bundles.rationale: Records remain authoritative only if their integrity is demonstrable, their accessibility is controlled and their disposition is defensible. composition.purpose: Specialises the parent knowledge-assertion model for the decision subject by adding decision-specific mandate, participation, approval and validity-state governance. Generic assertion identity, claim typing and evidential binding machinery stay in the parent and are not restated here.

Carries identifier-only references from decision content provenance to evidence records. Evidence identity, appraisal, quality grading and chain-of-custody semantics remain in the target; rationale-level evidence binding is owned by the reasoning area of this model.

Binds each approval, ratification or endorsement stage to the external activity record that evidences it. This model stores the binding identifier, stage code and outcome; activity initiation, assignment, execution and completion remain owned by the target.

Names the record that carries the decision and the authority that executes retention, transfer and destruction. This model states the retention binding, hold state, disposition authorisation and tombstone content; repository placement and physical execution remain owned by the target.
References a judicial or tribunal judgment that determines an appeal against the decision. Court composition, pleadings, orders, remedies and judicial reasoning are not modelled here.

Inbound relation: a change request is resolved by a decision. This model retains only the resolved change-request identifier and the resolution instant; change-request intake, triage, states and closure remain owned by the source model.

A decision may be constrained by, or may establish, a policy or executable rule. Only the reference, its binding role and any decision-specific parameters are held here; rule authoring, runtime evaluation, obligation discharge and enforcement remain external and are never inferred from the reference.

composition.target: ISO 15489-1:2016 records management concepts and principles
composition.purpose: Aligns authoritativeness, metadata, assigned responsibilities, records controls and appraisal-driven disposition. Alignment only: no conformance is claimed, since conformance depends on the adopting Dimension's records system and policy.

Maps attribution, qualified association with roles, delegation, revision, derivation and invalidation onto local provenance and delegation structures for interchange. Local semantics prevail where they diverge.

Maps in-force status, consolidation, amendment and repeal relations and authority attribution onto the local status and supersession model where the decision is a normative instrument. The ELI identifier, when assigned, ranks as a governed global identifier and does not displace the master-system identifier.

composition.target: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
composition.purpose: Maps issuer attribution, validity windows and revocation or suspension status onto the local authority and status model where a decision is projected as a verifiable credential. Credential formats and proof mechanisms remain a projection concern.

composition.target: OASIS Akoma Ntoso v1.0 Part 1 XML Vocabulary
composition.purpose: Maps FRBR-style work, expression, manifestation and item identification, lifecycle events, temporal data and top-level person, role and organisation references onto local version identity and participation structures for legislative and deliberative contexts.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one accountable decision-governance owner package and its owning organisational unit before any governance record is created; unowned governance records are invalid.

The owner package must publish the decision-rights or mandate catalogue it operates, the status vocabulary and permitted transitions, and the retention schedule authority under which it disposes of decision records.

The owner package must declare the jurisdictional profiles in force — at minimum the access-to-documents regime, the data-protection regime and any sector records legislation — and the local overrides each imposes on the default rules in this model.

The owner package must nominate a custodian for every stored projection and a reviewer or review forum for every decision class subject to periodic review, and must keep those nominations current through the role handover function.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable, dereferenceable namespace owned by the adopting Dimension, shaped as {dimension-base-iri}/decision-governance/{local-id}, where {local-id} is the master identifier or the Dimension-assigned ULID. Never encode a date, a status, an access class or an organisational unit into the namespace path, because all four change while identity must not. Where a governed global identifier such as an ELI-style legal identifier exists it is recorded as an alias and may be minted in its own namespace, but it never replaces the master identifier in the local namespace. Artefact-kind discriminators (GOVLED, GOVACC, GOVDIS) are part of the artefact name, not of the namespace.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-knw-010 for model identity, entry kind, status and review state
planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv for the authoritative relation ledger governing composition and ownership boundaries
The adopting Dimension's decision authority and delegation register, resolved through dr-gov-art-authority-register
The adopting Dimension's retention schedule register and its issuing records authority

canonicalization_rules: Serialize with deterministic member ordering and a declared character encoding; the digest in the integrity rule is computed over this canonical form and the canonical form must be named alongside the digest.

Normalise every timestamp to RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and retain the originally submitted offset as a separate field so that local civil time is not lost by normalisation.
Represent identifiers verbatim as issued by their master system, including case; do not case-fold, trim or re-pad a master identifier, and record any locally applied alias separately.
Store codes as code plus code-system reference; never store a display label as the value. Absent and empty are distinct: an absent field means not stated, an empty collection means stated as none.
patch_rules: The lifecycle ledger is append-only. Entries are never edited or removed; a correction is a new entry that references the entry it corrects and states the reason.

An approved or effective version is immutable. Substantive change is expressed by issuing a new version with a supersession reference, never by mutating the prior version; editorial correction to an approved version requires an erratum entry citing the authorising party.
Status changes only through the governed transition function, which validates the transition against the declared transition table and records acting authority, ground and effective instant.
Every patch carries the acting agent, the reason code, and both the event instant and the ingestion instant; a patch missing any of these is rejected.
Access classification and retention bindings are versioned, not overwritten: a reissued access schedule or disposition record increments its own zero-padded sequence and retains its predecessor.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional data element, an optional question or a new alignment is a minor, backward-compatible change.
Removing or narrowing a status value, an access class, a role or a code system, or making an optional element required, is breaking and requires a new major model version and a migration note.

Changing an alignment mapping is non-breaking where local semantics are unchanged; the alignment record must state the source version it maps to so that a target standard's revision does not silently alter local meaning.
Versioning applies to the model and to individual decision records independently: a model version change never rewrites the version identifiers of existing decision records.
Consumers must ignore unknown members rather than fail, but must not infer a default for an absent required element.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record for the decision — typically the deciding body's decision or minute register number — used verbatim as the decision master identifier and never re-minted locally.

Governed global identifier or IRI assigned by a recognised registry, such as an ELI-style legal identifier or another registry-governed IRI, used when no master-system identifier exists or recorded as an alias when one does.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, flagged as Dimension-assigned, used only when neither of the above exists; if a master identifier is later issued it is adopted as primary while the Dimension-assigned identifier is retained permanently as an alias.
A date, a meeting name, a title, an agenda item number, a file path or a bare sequence is never an identifier and must not be used as one, alone or in combination.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time values that include explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or the Z designator; a bare date, a date-time without seconds, and a date-time with no offset are all rejected. The offset -00:00 is used only where the instant in UTC is known but the local offset genuinely is not. Event time (when the governance act occurred, such as the decision being taken or a hold being imposed), observation time (when the fact was witnessed, attested or reported by a named party) and ingestion time (when the Vercy record captured it) are stored in separate fields and are never merged, back-filled from each other, or defaulted to the current clock; where a fact has only one meaningful time axis, the unused axes are left absent rather than duplicated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Every serial governance artefact is named {decision-master-identifier}-{artefact-kind}-{NNNN}: the decision master identifier resolved by the identity priority above, a fixed artefact-kind discriminator (GOVLED for the lifecycle and change ledger, GOVACC for the access and disclosure schedule, GOVDIS for the review, hold and disposition record), and NNNN, a zero-padded monotonic sequence whose scope is explicitly the decision master record. Sequences start at 0001, are never reused after supersession or deletion, and are never derived from a date, timestamp, retention year, review cycle or period label. A gap in a sequence must be explained by a lifecycle ledger entry. Non-serial artefacts, such as the authority and delegation register, take their identity from the identity priority instead and are keyed by authority plus mandate instrument.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each governed version and each serial artefact version records a named digest algorithm, the digest value computed over the declared canonical form, the sealing agent and the sealing instant, plus any signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidencing non-repudiation. Verification compares a retrieved projection against the stored digest and writes a verification outcome entry; a failure quarantines the projection and raises a notification, and the sealed version is never corrected in place. Vercy stores integrity values and references only: generating, protecting, reviewing and retaining audit trails, and enforcing any control derived from them, belong to the referenced records and audit systems.

policies: Authority before content: no decision record may reach an approved or effective status without a resolvable deciding authority and mandate binding whose validity window covers the decision event time.

Reference, do not reproduce: approval activities, carrying records, legal judgments, claims, evidence, policies and executable rules are held as identifiers with a binding role and decision-specific parameters only; their internal structures, lifecycles and operational functions are never mirrored here.

No local evaluation or enforcement: this model records assertions, classifications and instructions. Threshold evaluation, access enforcement, rule execution, obligation discharge and audit-trail generation are performed by external systems, and referencing such a system never transfers its semantics to this model.

Immutability after approval: approved and effective versions are immutable; change is expressed through new versions, supersession and append-only ledger entries, so that what was relied upon at a past instant remains reconstructable.

Tombstone-first disposition: content is superseded or tombstoned rather than erased unless an authorised erasure rule applies, and identity, authority, status and disposition facts survive every disposition that is not itself an authorised erasure of those facts.

Declared profiles, no global claims: jurisdiction-specific access, integrity and retention duties are recorded as named profiles or alignments; the model never asserts conformance to a standard or a legal regime without evidence recorded in the adopting Dimension.

read: Read is governed by the access classification held for each addressed part; the outcome, the rationale reference set and the governance metadata may carry different classes and are evaluated separately.

Register-level metadata declared in the discoverable metadata set — master identifier, subject reference, deciding authority and decision date — remains discoverable to authenticated readers even where content is withheld, unless a sensitive-item rule restricts the existence of the item itself.

Where an exemption covers only part of a record, readers receive the parts not covered, produced through the declared redaction profile; a partial release is recorded as a disclosure event in the lifecycle ledger.
Reads resolve references without dereferencing target-model content: a reader receives approval, evidence, record and judgment identifiers, not copies of those records.
Point-in-time reads must be answerable: given an instant, the reader can determine which version was authoritative and which status applied.
create: Only a party holding the governance owner or decision authority role may create a governance record, and creation must bind the decision master identifier, the deciding authority and the mandate reference.
Creation records the ingestion instant separately from the decision event instant, and a draft record must not carry an effective status or an effective instant.
A newly created record with no master-system identifier is minted a Dimension-assigned ULID that is flagged as such and retained as an alias if a master identifier later appears.
Creation opens the lifecycle ledger for the decision with an initial entry naming the creating agent, the capture mode and the source system where the record was imported or migrated.
update: Governance metadata on a draft may be updated in place; once a version is approved or effective it is immutable and change proceeds by new version and supersession reference.
Every update writes an append-only lifecycle ledger entry with acting agent, reason code, significance code and the separated event and ingestion instants; silent edits are rejected.
Status changes only through the governed transition function and only where the transition is permitted from the current status and the acting authority is competent for it.
Corrections to approved content are recorded as errata that cite the authorising party and leave the corrected version retrievable in its original sealed form.
No update may weaken an access classification or shorten a retention binding without a recorded authorisation from the classifying or records authority.
delete: Deletion is tombstone-first and supersession-first: superseding, revoking or expiring a decision never removes it, and content removal requires a disposition authorisation recorded in dr-gov-art-disposition-record.
Disposition is blocked while any legal hold or disposition freeze is in force, and while a review, appeal or reconsideration is open against the decision.

When an authorised disposition removes content, the surviving tombstone retains the decision master identifier and any aliases, the version identifier, the deciding authority reference, the status at disposition, the disposition action code, the disposition authorisation reference and the disposition instant, together with the lifecycle ledger entries that evidence the disposition.

Execution of destruction, transfer or migration is not performed by this model: it is owned by the carrying record model WM-REC-010 and the adopting Dimension's records authority operating under its published retention schedule, and this model records only the authorisation, the request and the evidence returned.

An authorised erasure rule — for example a data-protection erasure duty, subject to its own statutory exceptions for legal obligations, public-interest tasks, archiving and the defence of legal claims — may require removal of identifying content from the tombstone itself; where it applies, the erasure authorisation reference, its legal basis and the resulting reduced tombstone are recorded, and the surviving audit and integrity facts held by the external audit system are not deleted by this model.

Deletion of an entire lifecycle ledger, access schedule or disposition record is never permitted while the decision record exists; these artefacts are disposed of only as part of the decision's own authorised disposition.

roles.name: Decision authority
responsibilities: Take the decision within the mandate and record the authority and mandate binding
Attest satisfaction of the applicable decision rule and participation threshold
Authorise status transitions such as suspension, revocation and reopening
Determine whether a declared interest is disqualifying where the rules assign that determination to the chair or presiding office

roles.name: Governance owner
responsibilities: Own the decision record as a governed asset and account for its completeness
Maintain the authority and delegation register entries relied on by the decision
Approve role handovers and nominate custodians and reviewers
Declare the jurisdictional profiles applied to the record

roles.name: Records steward
responsibilities: Maintain the accuracy of governance metadata, including status, effective dating and version chain
Write and quality-check lifecycle ledger entries and errata
Bind the record to the correct retention schedule item and trigger
Prepare disposition requests and record the evidence returned

roles.name: Custodian
responsibilities: Hold and protect a stored projection of the record
Compute and store digests over the declared canonical form and report verification outcomes
Execute or relay disposition instructions to the executing records authority
Preserve tombstones and integrity references after content removal

roles.name: Reviewer or appeal forum
responsibilities: Conduct scheduled and triggered reviews by the recorded due instant
Receive appeals and reconsideration requests within the applicable window
Record the review outcome and its relation to the original decision without overwriting it
Refer matters to a judicial forum where the escalation tier requires it

roles.name: Access and disclosure authority
responsibilities: Set and revise access classifications and exemption grounds
Approve partial access and the redaction profile applied
Release the decision proactively when an embargo lapses
Apply personal-data minimisation before any disclosure

access.default_rule: Deny by default at finding and artefact scope. A reader obtains content only where an access class explicitly grants it for the addressed part; register-level metadata in the declared discoverable set is available to authenticated readers unless a sensitive-item rule restricts even the existence of the record. Enforcement is performed by the adopting Dimension's access-control system; this model supplies the classification and the disclosure instruction only.
exceptions: Proactive publication: once an embargo lapses and no hold or open appeal blocks release, the decision is published through the recorded channel by the named release authority.

Statutory access request: a request under an access-to-documents regime is answered by releasing the parts not covered by an exemption, applying the redaction profile, and giving written reasons for any refusal together with the available remedies.

Sensitive-item handling: items classified as sensitive are handled only by authorised personnel and are released only with the originating authority's consent, and their register references are worded so as not to disclose the protected content.
Legal hold and discovery access: a party conducting a hold or discovery obtains access for that purpose under a recorded authorisation, without altering the record's classification.

Emergency break-glass: an urgent operational need may be met by a time-boxed override that is recorded with the requester, the justification and the expiry instant, and that requires post-hoc ratification by the access and disclosure authority.
audit_requirements: Every access decision records the requester, the addressed scope, whether access was granted, refused or partial, and the exemption ground where refused or redacted.
Every break-glass override records its justification, its expiry instant and the outcome of its post-hoc ratification.
Disclosure events, embargo lapses and classification changes are written to the lifecycle ledger with separated event and ingestion instants.

Audit records themselves are generated, protected and retained by the external audit system identified in the audit trail reference; this model retains only the correlation identifier and a coverage note stating which governance acts are expected to appear there.

read_order: AGENTS.md first, to obtain Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any record
Specification URL, to load scope, boundaries, status vocabulary and permitted transitions
Relation ledger URL, to confirm which concepts are owned here and which belong to referenced models
Storage type URL, to learn the projection in use and its canonical form, whether that is a document store, a graph, a repository or a collection

Only then read or write records, resolving the decision master identifier before any artefact name is constructed

coverage.claim: This pass gives a defensible governance, participation and lifecycle structure for WM-KNW-010, grounded in twelve primary sources from eight independent organisations, and it deliberately stops at the boundaries of the core and reasoning areas of the same model and of the referenced approval, record, judgment, claim, evidence and policy models. It does not claim completeness for any jurisdiction, nor conformance to any cited standard.

checklist.notes: Identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier such as an ELI-style identifier, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID retained as an alias; dates, titles and agenda numbers are explicitly excluded. Serial artefacts derive names from the master identifier, a kind discriminator and a zero-padded sequence scoped to the decision record.

A controlled status vocabulary covers draft, submitted, approved, effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired and reopened with a transition table, competent authorities and separated approval, publication and effective instants. RFC 2026 supplies staged maturity, retirement and appeal precedent; ELI supplies in-force, consolidation and repeal relations.

Delegation chains, participant rosters, supersession and consolidation links, approval stage bindings and review outcome links are all typed references. Every outgoing relation is mirrored in the composition list with an explicit ownership statement.

All instants are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event, observation and ingestion times are separate fields; validity windows, embargo lapse, appeal windows and retention triggers are modelled explicitly. Retrospective effect is flagged where the effective instant precedes approval.

Attribution, derivation, attestation and capture mode align to PROV-O qualified patterns; the append-only ledger records acting agent, reason and authority for every governance act. Cited claims and evidence are identifier-only references.

Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer are distinguished, with handover events and residual accountability, and separated from the deciding authority that owns the substance. Six service-layer roles carry explicit responsibilities.

Quorum and decision-rule satisfaction is recorded as an attributed assertion by the presiding authority rather than computed here; integrity verification produces an outcome entry without mutating the sealed version; approval defects have codes and remediation paths.

Deny by default at all four scopes, per-part classification, exemption grounds with provision references, partial access by redaction, discoverable register metadata and five named exceptions including a ratified break-glass override. Enforcement is explicitly external.

Retention schedule binding with an explicit start trigger, legal hold blocking disposition, tombstone-first deletion with an enumerated surviving field set, named executing owner (WM-REC-010 and the Dimension records authority), archival transfer for permanent-value records, and an authorised-erasure path with its statutory exceptions.

Six alignments recorded as alignments only — ISO 15489-1, PROV-O, ELI 1.5, VC Data Model 2.0, Akoma Ntoso and NARA's requirement categories — each stating that local semantics prevail on divergence and that no conformance is claimed.

Mandate instrument, scope limits, validity window, succession and ultra vires handling are modelled, with the authority register as the resolution point. Grounded in ISO 15489-1 assigned responsibilities, ELI responsibility_of_agent and passed_by, and the Council's Rules of Procedure.

Participation mode, proxy representation and quorum attestation are grounded in Council Decision 2009/937/EU, which is jurisdiction-specific. No cross-domain primary standard was found for a conflict-of-interest register schema or for recusal effects on thresholds; the OECD conflict-of-interest guidance could not be retrieved during this pass, so this structure is marked as a gap rather than presented as canonical.

Digest algorithm and value over a declared canonical form, sealing agent, signature or timestamp-token reference, quarantine-on-failure and an external audit correlation identifier. Audit generation, protection and retention are stated as externally owned in line with the NIST control families.

Held only as identifier-only follow-up obligation references with the owning model named. Implementation progress, delivery data and outcome measurement are outside this model's boundary by design and no local structure is offered for them.

known_omissions: No controlled vocabulary is fixed for decision rules, recusal actions or reopening grounds; the adopting Dimension must publish one, and the codes here are placeholders bound to a code-system reference.

ISO 16175-1:2020 and the ISO 23081 metadata-for-records series were not directly consulted because their texts are paywalled; the records-metadata entity model, including an explicit mandate entity, is therefore inferred from ISO 15489-1 and NARA rather than from the most specific standard available.

The OECD guidance on managing conflict of interest in the public service could not be retrieved during this pass, so conflict-of-interest structure rests on a single EU procedural instrument and a data-protection instrument.
No structure is offered for meeting minutes or proceedings as such; where minutes exist they are referenced, and the model does not attempt to be a substitute account of a sitting.
Voting tallies are not modelled beyond an attested counted-and-required pair, because the dissent and objection content is owned by the reasoning area and a full ballot structure would duplicate it.
Cost, effort and resourcing consequences of a decision are not modelled at all; they belong to planning and financial models outside this boundary.
Cryptographic scheme profiles, key management and trust anchors are referenced but not specified; they belong to the adopting Dimension's security model.
conflicts: Records doctrine treats a captured record as fixed, while ELI and Akoma Ntoso treat a legal text as an expression that is consolidated and versioned over time. Resolved here by making versions immutable once approved and expressing all change as new versions with supersession links, so both readings hold, but adopters projecting to a records system that forbids multiple live expressions will need a profile.

A data-protection erasure duty can require removal of identifying content that a retention schedule and a legal hold require to be kept. The model's ordering — hold blocks disposition, and authorised erasure may reduce a tombstone — reflects the statutory exceptions for legal obligations, archiving and defence of legal claims, but the resolution is jurisdictional and must be decided by the adopting Dimension's records and privacy authorities, not by this model.

Verifiable-credential revocation semantics imply a status that can be flipped by the issuer at any time, whereas records doctrine requires the superseded state to remain retrievable. Resolved by treating credential status as a projection of the governed status, never as its master.

Access-to-documents regimes create a presumption of disclosure with enumerated exemptions, while security control catalogues start from deny-by-default. The model defaults to deny and treats proactive publication and statutory requests as recorded exceptions, which is conservative but will understate disclosure duties for public bodies unless the Dimension declares the access profile.

NARA's requirement set separates mandatory from preferred requirements for a records system, while this model states governance obligations for a decision record; an adopter should not read a 'Must Have' system requirement as satisfied merely because the corresponding governance field exists here.
regional_assumptions: Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001, Council Decision 2009/937/EU and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 are EU instruments used as profiles. They illustrate exemption grounds, partial access, quorum, proxy voting, written and silence procedures, storage limitation and erasure exceptions; they are not asserted to apply outside the EU.

NARA's Universal ERM Requirements and NIST SP 800-53 are United States federal profiles. Their requirement categories and control families inform structure but confer no obligation on non-US adopters.
ELI-style identifiers and Akoma Ntoso structures presume a legislative or deliberative context; for corporate or operational decisions they are optional alignments only.
No sources from Asia-Pacific, African, Latin American or Middle Eastern records or governance regimes were consulted in this pass, so region-specific duties there are unassessed.

The tiered appeal model drawn from RFC 2026 reflects one standards organisation's practice; statutory appeal rights, standing rules and time limits vary widely and must be supplied by the adopting Dimension.
adversarial_checks: Ownership sweep against the relation ledger: every bundle, layer, finding and function was re-read against the WM-ACT-032 and WM-KNW-008 rationales and against each outgoing reference. Approval execution, record disposal execution, evidence appraisal, claim structure, judicial reasoning, change-request lifecycle and rule evaluation were each found to be referenced only; where a draft concept drifted towards ownership — notably follow-up obligations and audit trails — it was reduced to an identifier-only reference and restated in out_of_scope or a boundary note.

Evaluation and enforcement test: the quorum function was deliberately renamed to attest rather than verify, and its effects state that no threshold computation or enforcement is performed. The integrity function verifies a digest but writes an outcome entry rather than acting on it, and the access layer emits classifications and instructions while enforcement is assigned to an external system.

Artefact collision test: the four artefacts introduced here (dr-gov-art-authority-register, dr-gov-art-lifecycle-ledger, dr-gov-art-access-schedule, dr-gov-art-disposition-record) were checked against the ten pre-existing core and reasoning artefact identifiers; none is re-created, renamed or shadowed, and dr-rsn-art-dissent-record is referenced by identifier only.

Identity falsifiability test: every artefact identity strategy and every local identifier was checked for date-derived or period-derived components. Serial names use a zero-padded sequence scoped to the decision master record, and the timestamp rule explicitly refuses bare dates, second-less times and offset-less times.

Exclusive representation test: each of the thirteen findings was checked to have either non-empty artefacts with a null rationale or an empty artefacts array with a substantive rationale; nine are inline-only with reasons that turn on reference-graph shape, personal-data minimisation or avoidance of duplicating an externally owned document.

Counterexample search for structure: a separate voting-record structure, a minutes artefact, an interests-register artefact and an implementation-tracking layer were each considered and rejected, because in every case an external owner already holds the concept and no primary source supported placing it here.
